statement: Top management approves a risk appetite statement, and it is turned into measurable tolerance limits, such as a maximum acceptable downtime or highest acceptable residual rating. The risk response options of accept, mitigate, transfer and avoid are defined, with criteria for choosing among them, including when outsourcing or cloud arrangements are acceptable. The risk method treats opportunities, the upside of risk, as a category alongside threats, and identified opportunities are recorded in risk decisions. All of this is communicated to risk owners and reviewed on a defined cycle. Proof is the approved statement, its version history and distribution records.
why_asked: Without stated limits, risk owners accept or reject risk by personal judgment and top management cannot tell whether exposure is within what it intended to carry.
how_to_ask: Ask for the appetite statement and look for limits a risk owner could measure against. Then ask how risk owners were told. Example probe: "What is the highest residual risk rating you will accept, who set it, and how does a risk owner know it?"
question: Does your organization have risk appetite and tolerance limits, approved by top management, that risk owners use to choose how to respond to risk?
expected_evidence: Approved risk appetite statement; risk tolerance statements with measurable limits; risk response criteria including acceptance and shared-responsibility conditions; distribution or briefing records for risk owners; version history showing the last review
good_looks_like: Top management has approved an appetite statement. Tolerance limits are measurable. The response options and the criteria for choosing among them are written, including conditions for outsourced and cloud arrangements. Opportunities are a named category in the method and appear in risk decisions. Risk owners received the statements and the statements carry a dated review.
test: Obtain the appetite and tolerance statements and the response criteria. Check top management approval, at least one measurable limit, response options with criteria for choosing among them including conditions for outsourced and cloud arrangements, opportunities named as a category in the method, and a review date within the organization's cycle. Sample three recent risk decisions and check identified opportunities are recorded in them. Sample three risk owners and check each received the statements. Pass if all checks hold.
baseline_risk: Risk is accepted inconsistently and exposure grows beyond what top management would knowingly choose.

statement: Cybersecurity and supply chain risks sit in the same enterprise risk process and register as other enterprise risks. The risk assessment method explicitly covers supplier risk, and supply chain security practices are part of the wider risk program. Enterprise risk reports to top management include these risks. Proof is the register, the method and the latest risk report.
why_asked: Security and supplier risks held in a separate list are never weighed against other business risks, and top management never sees them.
how_to_ask: Ask where cybersecurity and supplier risks are recorded, which method scores them, and whether they appear in the regular risk report. Example probe: "Show me where a supplier risk sits in the enterprise risk register and where it appears in the latest report to top management."
question: Does your organization manage security and supplier risks in its enterprise risk register?
expected_evidence: Enterprise risk register extract showing cybersecurity and supplier risks; risk assessment method covering supplier risk; risk management program description showing supply chain security as part of it; latest enterprise risk report to top management; covering the audit period.
good_looks_like: Cybersecurity and supplier risks share one register and one method with other enterprise risks, and the method names supplier risk. Supply chain security is part of the wider risk program. The latest risk report to top management includes these risks.
test: Obtain the enterprise risk register, the risk assessment method and the latest enterprise risk report to top management for the period. Check cybersecurity risks and supplier risks are in the same register as other enterprise risks and appear in the report. Check the method explicitly covers supply chain risk and the risk program references supply chain security practices. Pass if all hold.
baseline_risk: Security and supplier risks stay outside the enterprise risk view and are never traded off against other business risks.

statement: Departures from policy are approved through a defined exception process. Each exception needs a recorded approval and an expiry or review date. An exception register holds each open exception with who is accountable for it and its review date, and each exception is recorded with how it was handled. Proof is the register and the approval records.
why_asked: Open-ended waivers turn into permanent unmanaged risk, and nobody can show which departures from policy were approved or why.
how_to_ask: Ask for the exception register and look for open items without an accountable party or a date. Ask what happens when an exception expires. Example probe: "Show me an exception that expired in the last year. Who reviewed it and what was decided?"
question: Does your organization approve departures from policy through a defined exception process with an expiry or review date for each?
expected_evidence: Exception procedure; exception register with accountable parties, approvals, review dates and how each exception was handled; covering the audit period.
good_looks_like: Every exception has a recorded approval, someone accountable for it and an expiry or review date. Expired exceptions are closed or re-approved, and the register shows how each was handled. No exception is open-ended.
test: Obtain the exception procedure and the exception register for the period. Sample five open and closed exceptions and check each has a recorded approval, a recorded accountable party, an expiry or review date and a note of how it was handled. Pass if every sampled exception meets all four and none is open-ended.
baseline_risk: Policy waivers accumulate with no end date, so known weaknesses persist and cannot be defended to an auditor.

statement: The risk method requires internal and external threats, including insiders, to be identified. Identified threats are recorded in a threat register, or in the risk register, and the entries are updated from threat intelligence on a defined cycle. Proof is the method, the register and its version history.
why_asked: Risk ratings built on an outdated or incomplete threat picture understate exposure to the attacks actually in play.
how_to_ask: Ask for the threat register and how it is updated. Look for insider threats and recent changes. Example probe: "Which threats were added or changed after your last threat intelligence review, and where did that information come from?"
question: Does your organization keep a current register of internal and external threats, including insiders?
expected_evidence: Risk assessment method requiring threat identification; threat register or risk register with internal, insider and external threats; version history showing updates from threat intelligence; covering the audit period
good_looks_like: The method requires threats to be identified. The register lists internal, insider and external threats. Entries were updated in the period from named intelligence sources.
test: Obtain the method, the register and its version history. Check the method requires threat identification and the register lists internal and external threats including insiders. Sample three entries and check at least one update in the period cites threat intelligence. Pass if all hold.
baseline_risk: New attack methods go unrecognized, so risk assessments miss the threats most likely to occur.

statement: Written criteria set when a cybersecurity risk is escalated into enterprise risk management. Defined channels exist for raising and escalating security risk across the organization, and they cover risk that starts with suppliers and other third parties. Risks that meet the threshold are routed through those channels, and material supply chain risks reach top management. Proof is the criteria, the channel description and escalation records.
why_asked: Without written criteria and working channels, serious security and supplier risks stay with whoever noticed them and never reach those who can decide.
how_to_ask: Ask for the written escalation criteria and the channel description, then ask for a real case. Check the channels cover suppliers. Example probe: "Walk me through the last supplier risk that met the escalation threshold and who received it."
question: Does your organization define channels and criteria for escalating security risks, including supplier risks?
expected_evidence: Risk escalation criteria; description of escalation channels including supplier risk; escalation records showing the recipient; records of material supply chain risks reaching top management; covering the audit period.
good_looks_like: Escalation criteria are written and say when a risk moves into enterprise risk management. Channels are documented from staff upward and explicitly cover supplier and third-party risk. At least one risk in the period was escalated through a channel and reached the intended recipient, including a material supply chain risk.
test: Obtain the escalation criteria, the channel description and the escalation records for the period. Check the criteria state when a risk is escalated and the channels cover supplier and third-party risk. Sample three risks that met the threshold and check each was routed through a defined channel and reached the intended recipient. Check a material supply chain risk was escalated to top management in the period. Pass if all hold.
baseline_risk: Material security and supplier risks are never escalated, so decisions about them are made too low or not at all.
